newsitem.title: UK: Closing overseas stock market indices.
newsitem.headline: Closing overseas stock market indices.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - Britain's leading stock index ended moderately higher as Abbey National lifted the banking sector and a weaker pound breathed new life into engineering stocks, traders and analysts said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,876.6, up 14.0 points, or 0.29 percent.

FRANKFURT - German stocks ended market trade slightly firmer but off session peaks as dealers said the market was searching for direction after the recent advance to new all-time record levels. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,381.69, up 10.53 points, or 0.24 percent. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,377.70, down 22.60 points, or 0.51 percent.
PARIS - French stocks finished slightly higher, settling just below Friday's record close, after a quiet session. The CAC-40 index closed at 3,023.63, up 1.43 points, or 0.05 percent.
ZURICH - Swiss stocks ended lower in nervous trade as profit-taking and derivatives-linked selling put on pressure. The Swiss market index closed at 5,842.1, down 45.9 points, or 0.78 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower, snapping a three-session winning streak, as an earlier rally based on blue-chip stocks yielded to profit-taking, brokers said. The 225-stock Nikkei average closed at 20,402.74, down 172.52 points, or 0.84 percent.

SYDNEY - A polished performance from the gold sector led the Australian stock market to a stronger close, although gains were trimmed in the afternoon. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,731.9, up 8.1 points, or 0.30 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended at a record closing high with virtually all market attention focused on blue-chip conglomerate Hutchison Whampoa, which continued a record-breaking rally. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,772.06, up 105.47 points, or 0.67 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial stocks ended down as disappointment spurred by poor June private-sector credit extension data dashed hopes of an imminent interest rate cut. The All-Stock index closed at 7,473.8, down 17.0 points, or 0.23 percent. The All-Gold index closed at 986.5, down 4.3 points, or 0.43 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9,105.3, down 20.6 points, or 0.23 percent.
